claim: T cells are required to clear infection.

claim: Naive T cells move within the paracortex of the lymph node.
source: Prior to infection, naive T cells move within the paracortex of the lymph node (LN), and upon interaction with cognate antigen bearing dendritic cells (Miller et al., 2004), T cells activate and effector CD8 T cells move to peripheral tissue sites of infection.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Miller et al., 2004.

claim: Despite large differences amongst individual T cell movements within any specific tissue, the overall patterns of T cell motility remain similar within tissue and across tissues.
source: However, despite large differences amongst individual T cell movements within any specific tissue, the overall patterns of T cell motility remain similar within tissue and across tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of data with and without outlier frames.

claim: The low confinement of naive T cells in the LN environment may contribute to the high meandering ratio.
source: The low confinement of naive T cells in the LN environment may contribute to the high meandering ratio while confinement as well as antigen in the lung (Flu) likely decrease the ability of T cells to move directionally (Figure 4) and lead to low meandering ratios.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data on confinement and meandering ratio.

claim: Confinement as well as antigen in the lung (Flu) likely decrease the ability of T cells to move directionally and lead to low meandering ratios.
source: The low confinement of naive T cells in the LN environment may contribute to the high meandering ratio while confinement as well as antigen in the lung (Flu) likely decrease the ability of T cells to move directionally (Figure 4) and lead to low meandering ratios.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data on confinement, antigen presence, and meandering ratio.

claim: The volume patrolled by a T cell is dependent not only on its speed but also on turning angles, the cell's tendency to meander, and the amount of time the cell spends confined to a location.
source: The volume patrolled by a T cell is dependent not only on its speed but also on turning angles, the cell's tendency to meander, and the amount of time the cell spends confined to a location.
evidence: This is a statement about the factors that contribute to volume patrolled, based on the analysis presented.

claim: Tissue environments may contribute to different modes of T cell movement, which can impact the efficiency of T cell searches for target cells in tissues.
source: Our results suggest that tissue environments may contribute to different modes of T cell movement, which can impact the efficiency of T cell searches for target cells in tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined analysis of all motility parameters across tissues.

claim: We previously found no difference in motility speed and patterns of naive CD4 and CD8 T cells in LNs.
source: We previously found no difference in motility speed and patterns of naive CD4 and CD8 T cells in LNs (Fricke et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fricke et al., 2016.

claim: We normalized time steps to 90 s for all data sets.
source: To ensure consistency across analyses, we normalized time steps to 90 s for all data sets (for details, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study.

claim: Effector T cells in the villi move slightly faster at d8 compared to d5.
source: A direct comparison of effector T cells moving d5 versus d8 post infection in the villi show that some motility parameters remain similar, including persistence (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). Effector T cells in the villi move slightly faster at d8 compared to d5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B), likely reflecting decreasing antigen load with clearance of virus at later times post infection.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: The faster speed at d8 compared to d5 likely reflects decreasing antigen load with clearance of virus at later times post infection.
source: Effector T cells in the villi move slightly faster at d8 compared to d5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, B), likely reflecting decreasing antigen load with clearance of virus at later times post infection.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data and knowledge of viral clearance kinetics.
